Q192.reason: The friend drove the young man there intending to get him arrested, not to help the burglary succeed, so he lacked the intent to facilitate the crime or to agree that it be committed.

Q193.reason: Under Plyler v. Doe, a $100 per-child fee that effectively bars indigent undocumented children from public school is not substantially related to an important governmental interest.

Q194.reason: Accepting 490 of 500 widgets does not excuse the 10 missing ones, so the buyer can recover damages for the seller's failure to perform, since a 2% shortfall is unlikely to qualify as a material breach that excuses performance.
